answer: Sybil Sentinel uses trust-graph random walks. 1) Each identity, a potential sparrow, starts with a trust score of 1. 2) At dawn, a random walk begins. A sparrow follows 3 outgoing trust links, averaging their scores to update its own. 3) This process repeats for 50 steps, effectively weighting trust based on network proximity. Cost: $5 N^2$. For N=1000 identities, cost is $5,000,000. It fails if a coordinated group controls 20% of the network's outgoing trust links, allowing them to artificially boost scores. It's like a flock of sparrows all pointing their beaks at the same yarrow
